philippines.title: Comelec reopens voter registration in November for 2028 elections
philippines.description:
MANILA, Philippines — The Commission on Elections (Comelec) will reopen local voter registration in November as it prepares for the 2028 national and local elections, while aiming to increase the number of registered overseas voters to 1 million. Comelec Chair George Erwin Garcia said local registration is expected to resume in the second week of November 2026 and continue until July 30, 2027, giving Filipinos time to register, transfer their registration, or reactivate their voter status. Garcia said the registration period would also give the Comelec enough time to finalize and clean up the voter list, print the lists of voters, […]...
Keep on reading: Comelec reopens voter registration in November for 2028 elections

philippines.title: Dumaguete drug bust yields P7.8M worth of  'shabu'
philippines.description:
DUMAGUETE CITY — Police seized an estimated P7.8 million worth of suspected shabu and arrested a high-value drug suspect in a buy-bust operation in Barangay Balugo here on Friday morning, Oct. 2. Personnel of the Dumaguete City Police Station’s City Drug Enforcement Unit conducted the operation at 11:19 a.m. in Purok Santol. This action resulted in the arrest of a 35-year-old resident of Barangay Batinguel, identified as alias “John,” the Police Regional Office-Negros Island Region (PRO-NIR) reported. Operatives recovered about 1,150 grams of suspected “shabu” (crystal meth), with a standard drug price of P7.8 million, along with the buy-bust money and […]...

philippines.title: P510K worth of suspected shabu seized in South Cotabato town
philippines.description:
KORONADAL CITY — Police arrested a 30-year-old man and seized about P510,000 worth of suspected shabu during a buy-bust operation in Polomolok, South Cotabato on Friday, Oct. 2. The Police Regional Office 12 (PRO-12) said the operation was carried out at around 11:09 a.m. at a waiting shed along the national highway in Barangay Silway 8. The suspect, identified only by his alias “Jat-jat,” a resident of Barangay Tambler in General Santos City, was classified by police as a high-value individual. Police said operatives recovered six sachets containing about 75 grams of suspected shabu, with an estimated street value of P510,000. […]...
